That stomach-drop every time her door opens is the real thing keeping you up—not the duplex. The duplex is just the thing you can put a red star next to. The boss thing has no binder, no porch, no clear shape, so it just sits there.

And saying “everything is fine” wasn’t you being an idiot. It’s the reflex when someone with power over your job pulls you aside and you don’t know what’s coming. Your body went into threat mode and you picked the safest word. The problem is now the ambiguity is doing more damage than the conversation would have.

The useful question isn’t “why am I going Thursday”—it’s “what did she actually say?” Because “watching me” can mean three very different things: she’s concerned about performance, she’s checking in because she noticed the overtime, or she’s managing you more closely for reasons that have nothing to do with you. Your nervous system is treating all three as the same.

If you can, go back to her with something small and honest, not a confession: “I’ve been thinking about our conversation. I said I was fine, but I want to make sure I understand what you’re seeing and what would help.” That gives her a chance to be specific—and gives you something real to react to instead of the door opening.

What did she actually say when she pulled you aside?
